references: The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Detroit Pistons, 115 - 92, at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday evening. The Bucks (16 - 7) came in well - rested, last having taken the court Saturday. That energy was evident in the first half, as Milwaukee had forged a 56 - 45 lead over the Pistons (13 - 9) by intermission. The home squad would keep the pressure on in the second half, compiling another 59 points while limiting Detroit to 47. The Bucks put on a stellar offensive show, holding the visitors to 36 percent shooting and forcing 20 turnovers. Blake Griffin's 31 points, which he supplemented with seven rebounds, four assists and one block, led the Pistons. Reggie Jackson provided 15 points, seven rebounds, five assists and one steal. Andre Drummond continued a string of quiet games with 10 points, eight boards, one assist and one steal. No other Detroit player hit double digits in the scoring column, with Zaza Pachuilia coming the closest with eight points off the bench. Eric Bledsoe paced the Bucks with 27 points, adding four assists, three rebounds and four steals. Giannis Antetokounmpo managed 15 points, eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Malcolm Brogdon poured in 14 points and also supplied six rebounds and two assists. Tony Snell drew a start for Khris Middleton (personal) and netted 11 points, seven rebounds, one assist and two steals. Thon Maker and Sterling Brown delivered matching 11 - point tallies off the bench. The Pistons head back home and tangle with the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night, while the Bucks remain home for a Friday night showdown against the Golden State Warriors.
